sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Light Value-Added Postponement Packaging and Custom Kitting

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil law (continental European, unitary state; codified commercial law in the Code de commerce; dual judicial and administrative court system)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between France and China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (signed 30 May 1984, amended by the 2013 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monetaire et financier (CMF) Articles L. 561-1 et seq. and R. 561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT duties and beneficial owner register); CMF Articles L. 561-45 to L. 561-57 (RBE declaration of beneficial owners); Code de commerce Articles L. 123-1 to L. 123-12 and R. 123-167 (registry, INPI Guichet unique, domiciliation); Ordonnance No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 and Decret No. 2021-582 of 11 May 2021 (transposition of Directive (EU) 2018/843); Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (future EU AML rulebook, phase-in from 2027); ACPR guidelines on beneficial-owner identification; post-CJEU Case C-37/20 (Sovim, 22 November 2022) restrictions on public access to the beneficial ownership file.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarial copy of passport or national identity card of each shareholder and of the appointed SAS President
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent authority of the shareholder's country of nationality

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, articles of association and current registry extract (K-bis equivalent) of any legal entity shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the French incorporation agent and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter evidencing source of funds of each shareholder (source-of-wealth control)
Registered-office occupancy certificate (attestation de domiciliation) issued by the licensed French domiciliation company or lessor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed French domiciliation company or lessor of the registered office in France
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic French document; no apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under CMF Article L. 561-5 for all shareholders, directors and beneficial owners, using a zero-false-negative screening protocol against TRACFIN guidance, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, French national asset-freeze measures (CMF Article L. 562-1 et seq.), and politically exposed person (PEP) databases as defined in CMF Article L. 561-10. The low-risk standard tier for kitting and 3PL commerce permits simplified due diligence measures but does not waive identification, verification and UBO declaration duties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet unique des formalites d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), which transmits the incorporation file to the greffe du tribunal de commerce for RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Societes) registration; pre-filing name screening is conducted through INPI Data (data.inpi.fr) and infogreffe.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (denomination sociale) must be written in Latin-script characters; all statutory filings, legal announcements and mandatory documents must be drafted in French under the Toubon Law (loi No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994). Non-Latin-script word elements require an official Latin-script transliteration filed as the registered name. The name must be lawful, available, not misleading, and free of conflict with prior trademark or company-name rights.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANQUE / CREDIT (reserved for ACPR-licensed credit institutions)
ASSURANCE / ASSUREUR (reserved for ACPR-licensed insurance undertakings)
REPUBLIQUE / PRESIDENCE / PREFECTURE (reserved to the State)
POLICE / GENDARMERIE / DOUANE (reserved to public authorities)
CROIX-ROUGE / RED CROSS / RED CRESCENT (protected emblems under the Geneva Conventions)
UNION EUROPEENNE / EUROPEAN UNION (may not imply official EU institution status)
SOCIETE GENERALE / BNP PARIBAS and other well-known marks (trademark and company-name infringement risk)
SAS / SA / SARL (legal-form suffixes that misstate the actual SAS status are prohibited)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France operates no standalone pre-incorporation name reservation system; the name is protected upon RCS registration or earlier INPI trademark filing. The 30-day window is the internal validity period of the pre-filing availability search. Upon rejection: (1) the greffe issues a reasoned non-registration notice; (2) the applicant may correct and immediately re-file through the INPI Guichet unique or, within 15 days, contest the refusal by summary request (requete) to the President of the Tribunal de commerce or Tribunal judiciaire to compel registration; (3) where third-party trademark rights are asserted, the applicant may file an opposition under Article L. 712-4 of the Code de la propriete intellectuelle within two months of trademark publication, or bring infringement and passing-off proceedings in the civil courts, while preserving settlement options.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual-style registered office is permissible only through a duly licensed commercial domiciliation company (societe de domiciliation agreée) satisfying Code de commerce Articles L. 123-11-1 and R. 123-167: the provider must hold prefectoral authorization, maintain a physical address in France, and receive and forward official mail. A bare post-office box or non-physical mailbox is non-compliant. Given the fulfillment and kitting activity, the SAS must complement the domiciled registered office with the physical operating warehouse declared as a separate establishment so as to evidence real commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 12% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection for an established low-risk 3PL kitting site, driven mainly by URSSAF social-contribution audits, DREETS/DDETSPP labour inspections, and French Customs (Douane) verification of stored goods and intra-EU inventory movements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability search and INPI data and trademark screening (warehousing and logistics classes)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI and licensed IP screening agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: INPI online data is free; USD 120 is the prevailing market rate for a formal availability and confusingly-similar mark report covering the business description.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Guichet unique (INPI) incorporation filing duty and fixed RCS registrar fee (droit de greffe)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI Guichet unique / greffe du tribunal de commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed tariff of approximately EUR 38-48 (USD 45-52) for creating a commercial legal entity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the mandatory legal announcement (annonce legale) in an authorized journal in the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed legal journal publisher (journal d'annonces legales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 150-220 (USD 165-240) per insertion for a SAS incorporation notice, varying by department and gazette.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation service, first 12 months, including mail reception and forwarding
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 45-60 per month (USD 49-65) for a business center with physical presence, scanning and mail-forwarding services.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC and UBO identification file - PEP, OFAC, EU, UN and TRACFIN-linked sanctions screening of each shareholder and beneficial owner
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance service provider / SAS incorporation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a standard low-risk-tier corporate KYC remediation file covering beneficial-owner verification and comprehensive sanctions-list screening.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified legal translation of non-French shareholder identity documents and corporate extracts into French
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing local tariff of EUR 0.25-0.35 per standard line plus certification fee; estimate for two shareholder files of approximately eight pages.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille or consular legalization fee per corporate shareholder document
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority of the country of origin (France: apostille issued free of charge; China: Ministry of Foreign Affairs or entry-exit authority at RMB 100-200) or French consulate for consular path
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Estimated at USD 65 per document including the fixed official levy, agency handling and courier.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of the SAS statuts (articles of association), President's acceptance and UBO statement, reviewed by a French avocat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French law firm (avocat at the bar)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee of EUR 650-950 (USD 700-1,025) for a standard SAS incorporation file, excluding notarial acts.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Capital-deposit certificate (attestation de depot de fonds) issued by a bank or Caisse des Depots et Consignations for subscribed share capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Deposit-taking bank or Caisse des Depots et Consignations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 0-50 for issuance of the deposit attestation and opening of the temporary capital account; estimated at USD 45 with expedited handling.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (SAS), and related provisions on registration (L.227-1, L.227-9, L.227-10, R.227-1 et seq.)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) of the registered office's jurisdiction
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and M0 form (or via the Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum capital required for SAS; capital freely set in Articles. At least 50% of nominal value of cash contributions must be paid up at incorporation; in-kind contributions fully paid up. No escrow account required unless capital is in kind.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders hereby adopt the Articles of Association of the Company as presented; that the share capital of €[X] is subscribed and paid in as per the terms; that the registered office is established at [address]; that [Name] is appointed President, [Name] as General Manager, and [Name] as Secretary; that the President is authorized to execute all documents and filings necessary for incorporation, including publication of legal notice and registration with the Commercial Court Registry; and that all actions taken by the founders in furtherance of incorporation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional unless real estate contribution) or private deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts (Articles) in French, including corporate name, registered office address, corporate purpose (kitting, packaging, warehousing), share capital, share classes, governance rules, and appointment of first President. All shareholders must sign. If a notary is used, notarization is required for contributions of real estate or certain in-kind assets.
required_dossiers: Proof of address for registered office (lease or ownership title)
Bank certificate of capital deposit (if cash contributions)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the Articles, amend and re-sign; if notarization is required, schedule a notary appointment and correct any omissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Legal Notice in a Journal of Legal Announcements (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorized in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice containing the company name, form (SAS), capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, and the identity of the President. The notice must be published within 8 days of signing the Articles. Obtain a certificate of publication (attestation de parution).
required_dossiers: Proof of payment for publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the notice, correct the information and republish; ensure the notice meets legal content requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Dossier with the Commercial Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via the Guichet des Formalités des Entreprises online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation file electronically through the official portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr). Include the signed Articles, legal notice publication certificate, proof of registered office, capital deposit certificate (if applicable), and identification of the President. The registry will review and issue a Kbis extract upon approval.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office (lease or utility bill)
Declaration of non-conviction for the President (form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query (e.g., missing document), respond within 15 days via the portal; correct and resubmit the deficient item. If rejected, appeal to the President of the Commercial Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Kbis Extract and SIRET Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INSEE (National Institute of Statistics)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, the registry issues the Kbis (official company extract) and the SIRET number is automatically assigned. The Kbis serves as proof of legal existence and must be displayed at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is delayed, contact the registry; verify that all filings were complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Social Security and Tax Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF (social security) and Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company is automatically registered for social security (URSSAF) upon incorporation. For tax, the company must file an initial tax return (form 1477) and register for VAT (if applicable) via the DGFiP. The President must also be registered as a corporate officer.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, contact URSSAF or DGFiP directly; ensure all forms are correctly filed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS) – for workplace safety and occupational permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General business registration (Kbis) and compliance with local zoning; no specific operating license required for kitting/fulfillment activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique (via DREETS – Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Déclaration) under ICPE (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) if storage capacity exceeds 500 m² or if certain thresholds are met; otherwise exempt
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with French Environmental Code (Code de l'environnement) for wastewater discharge limits (e.g., pH 5.5-8.5, COD < 125 mg/L), VOC emissions limits (if applicable), and proper waste management (tri and disposal via certified channels)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire department (SDIS) for premises > 300 m²; structural load inspection for racking systems; workplace health and safety clearance from DREETS (including emergency exits, ventilation, and ergonomic assessments)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), administered through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official impots.gouv.fr portal. Corporate registration data and business identifiers are also coordinated through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is incorporated through the Guichet unique with submission of its articles, registered office details, directors, beneficial-owner information, activity description, and supporting identification documents. The INPI process transmits the filing to the competent registries and tax authorities. The entity receives a SIREN number for the legal entity and a SIRET number for each establishment. The DGFiP allocates the French intra-Community VAT identification number, generally consisting of the country prefix FR, a two-digit key, and the nine-digit SIREN number. The SAS must provide its legal, banking, activity, premises, and expected turnover information to the SIE and request VAT activation where required. A foreign entity without a French establishment applies through the designated non-established-business tax service of the DGFiP for French VAT registration, submitting its certificate of incorporation, foreign tax registration, constitutional documents, proof of business activity, identity of authorized representatives, and evidence of taxable transactions. Businesses established in another EU Member State may use the applicable Union OSS regime for eligible intra-Community distance sales and specified B2C services, but OSS does not replace ordinary French VAT registration where French domestic transactions, imports, stock, or establishment-related obligations require it.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). A qualifying closely held SAS may elect temporary taxation under the income-tax partnership-style regime under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code, generally for a maximum period of five fiscal years and subject to conditions concerning ownership, voting rights, size, age, and operating activity. The election is not a general United States-style check-the-box election and is not available solely by filing a classification form. France has anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implementing the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive, including limitations on deductions and denial of duplicate deductions or deductions without corresponding inclusion; these rules do not provide a general elective hybrid classification. VAT franchise, real-tax, and simplified reporting regimes are compliance regimes rather than entity-classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French value added tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or TVA), integrated into the EU VAT system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For the French VAT franchise regime, the principal annual turnover threshold is EUR 37,500 for services and non-commercial activities and EUR 85,000 for goods, accommodation, and certain mixed activities. Increased thresholds are generally EUR 41,250 for services and EUR 93,500 for goods. A fulfillment, kitting, and packaging operator must classify each transaction based on its economic substance; services involving customer-owned goods generally follow the services thresholds, while sales of packaged or assembled goods may follow the goods thresholds. Exceeding the applicable threshold or voluntarily opting for ordinary VAT taxation triggers VAT charging, filing, invoicing, and deduction obligations. Imports, intra-Community acquisitions, domestic stock, and other transaction-specific rules can create registration obligations independently of the franchise thresholds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is introducing mandatory domestic B2B electronic invoicing and transaction reporting in phases. From 1 September 2026, all businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices; large and medium-sized enterprises are generally required to issue domestic B2B electronic invoices from that date. Small and micro-enterprises are generally required to issue them from 1 September 2027. Electronic invoices must be exchanged through an approved private platform (plateforme de dématérialisation partenaire, or PDP) or the designated public infrastructure as legally available. France uses a structured exchange and data-reporting model rather than a universal real-time pre-clearance system for every invoice. E-reporting of specified B2C and foreign transactions is phased with the same timetable. Invoices must contain mandatory French and EU VAT particulars, including supplier and customer identification, VAT numbers where applicable, invoice date and unique sequential number, taxable amount, rate, VAT amount, currency, payment terms, and applicable reverse-charge or exemption references. Electronic customs systems and EDI/API interfaces may be required for export declarations and customs data, but customs data exchange is distinct from VAT invoice clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the EU may be invoiced without French VAT where the goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU by the supplier or by the customer acting under the applicable conditions, and the supplier retains prescribed evidence of export and exit from the EU customs territory. The export must be reported under the correct customs procedure and linked to the commercial invoice and transport records. Intra-Community supplies of goods to a VAT-identified customer in another EU Member State may qualify for VAT exemption, subject to valid customer VAT identification, transport evidence, recapitulative reporting, and transaction-level documentation. B2B services supplied to a business established outside France generally follow the customer-location rule and are outside the scope of French VAT rather than technically zero-rated exports; the supplier must retain evidence of the customer's business status and location. Services directly connected with export transactions may qualify for specific VAT exemptions where statutory conditions are met. Export VAT refunds require valid purchase invoices, business-use evidence, deductible-tax eligibility, customs and transport records where relevant, and timely submission through the applicable French or EU refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration filed through the applicable French customs system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs exit confirmation or equivalent electronic proof that the goods exited the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, Incoterms, and VAT treatment
Packing list and detailed description of the kitted or packaged goods
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or courier export record
Warehouse, fulfillment, assembly, and stock-movement records linking the exported goods to the customer order
Proof of delivery or receipt outside the EU where available and relevant
Customer order, contract, and purchase documentation
Evidence of customer location and, for intra-Community supplies, the customer's valid VAT identification number
Accounting records, VAT returns, export sales ledger, and reconciliation between invoices, customs declarations, and transport documents
Bank payment records or other commercial payment evidence where relevant; French law does not generally require an inward-remittance certificate as a universal export zero-rating condition
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Export zero-rating or exemption may be denied and French VAT reassessed where the supplier cannot prove dispatch or transport outside the EU, customs exit, customer status, transaction substance, or accurate reporting. The reassessed VAT is generally accompanied by late-payment interest, ordinarily calculated at 0.20% per month under the French Tax Code, subject to applicable statutory rules. Tax penalties may include a 10% surcharge for late or deficient payment, a 40% surcharge for deliberate failure, and an 80% surcharge for fraudulent conduct or abusive manoeuvres, with specific rules and procedural safeguards applying. Incorrect invoices may expose the issuer to liability for VAT shown or improperly deducted. In addition, input VAT refunds may be rejected or clawed back, and customs duties or import VAT may be reassessed where customs declarations are inaccurate. Serious intentional fraud may trigger criminal proceedings, fines, and imprisonment under applicable French law. The taxpayer must preserve reliable records for the applicable statutory retention period, generally at least six years for tax documentation, with longer periods potentially applying to accounting, customs, or commercial records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting in coordination with the Direction Generale du Tresor for balance-of-payments and foreign-exchange statistical administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies full current-account and capital-account convertibility under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. The euro is freely convertible, and no prior foreign-exchange approval is required for capital contributions, trade settlements, or profit remittances by an SAS. Dividend and profit remittance hurdles are documentary only: distributable profits must be evidenced by filed annual accounts, the paying bank may request a French tax residence certificate, and reduced treaty-withholding relief requires the appropriate attestation from the French and foreign tax authorities. There are no quantitative remittance caps, but all reportable cross-border payments must be identified to Banque de France, generally through the authorized bank's balance-of-payments declaration system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no compulsory conversion ratio in France. Export receivables may be retained indefinitely in any convertible currency or in EUR, with a mandatory conversion ratio of 0%. Export transactions are not subject to repatriation deadlines, but the receiving bank must capture the transaction for French balance-of-payments statistical reporting where the monthly or annual reporting thresholds apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE S.A. (Banque Populaire / Caisse d'Epargne corporate desk)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. French and EEA-licensed electronic money institutions are suitable supplementary rails for cross-border FX, low-value disbursements, and vendor payments, provided they hold a valid ACPR authorization or a PSD2 passport into France. Offshore non-EEA digital EMIs without an EU passport cannot lawfully service the French market as a primary bank, cannot issue French IBANs, and cannot be used for the SAS's statutory corporate account; they may only function as payment-orchestration or virtual-account technology layers through an authorized partner bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate account opening is legally permitted under ACPR digital-identity and e-signature guidance, and a physical visit to a French branch is not an explicit statutory condition. In practice, most Tier-1 banks require a live video interview with every director and natural-person UBO, presentation of original passports, proof of address, and electronic signature of the bank mandate. Foreign-owned SAS structures often receive a soft in-person meeting condition for final sign-off, and all foreign corporate documents must be apostilled/legalized and translated into French where requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of ultimate beneficial ownership through non-EU intermediaries or multi-layer corporate chains
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized UBO declaration with full ownership percentages; constitutional documents and commercial-registry extracts for each intermediary; certified passports of all UBOs; source-of-wealth letters with bank references; sanctions and PEP screening reports for every connected director and beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or shareholders requesting remote signing authority
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled board resolutions creating bank mandates; certified directors' passports and proof of address; current Kbis extract; notarized or apostilled powers of attorney; tax residency certificates; bank-specific director and UBO questionnaires completed in French or English.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a jurisdiction perceived as high-risk or non-transparent
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed share subscription agreement; bank statements of the transferring party showing cleared source of funds; SEPA or SWIFT transfer proof; French balance-of-payments direct-investment classification reference; shareholder tax declaration or equivalent; auditor's or depository bank certificate where a capital escrow account is used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Significant trade-payable mismatch or 3PL aggregate settlement flows with unidentified downstream beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed fulfillment and kitting customer contracts; commercial invoices and order-management reports; warehouse inventory reconciliation; transport documents, including CMRs; downstream customer UBO/KYC records where maintained by the 3PL; AML transaction questionnaire describing the full physical and financial supply chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of fintech or virtual-account aggregators causing co-mingling or non-bank exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Reconciliation ledger for every virtual account or sub-account; treasury system reports; Airwallex or equivalent EMI wallet statements; evidence of the EMI's ACPR authorization or passport and its client-fund safeguarding arrangements; confirmations that settlement flows are ultimately routed to the SAS's primary French bank account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must be routed exclusively through cleared and fully identified bank channels. For EEA or SEPA shareholders, use EUR SEPA Credit Transfer to the SAS's French IBAN. For non-SEPA shareholders, use SWIFT MT103 with the French receiving bank as beneficiary bank, including a genuine remitter, the SAS's legal name and Kbis-matched beneficiary identifier, and the French balance-of-payments purpose classification for direct investment or equity participation. The remittance reference must state 'Capital subscription - SAS [name] - transaction number'. The bank will require the capital subscription deed and, where funds are first placed in escrow, the depository certificate before releasing funds to the operational account. No anonymous cash or third-party pass-through settlement is acceptable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade payments for fulfillment and kitting assembly should use: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for EUR payments to EU suppliers; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA or non-EUR disbursements, with beneficiary name, IBAN, and remittance details matching the underlying purchase order and commercial invoice; and (iii) irrevocable import documentary credits governed by ICC UCP 600 for high-value packaging machinery, tooling, or bulk material purchases where the supplier requires a bank payment undertaking. Supporting documents must include purchase order, commercial invoice, packing list, proof of delivery or CMR, and, where requested, final-consignee certificates for dual-use or controlled logistics inputs. Fintech payout rails may be used for low-value disbursements only after pre-funding from the French operational account and must remain fully reconcilable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards in EUR/USD and EUR/CNH for forecast commercial cash flows
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) solely for restricted or non-convertible currencies where no offshore deliverable market exists
EUR cross-currency swaps for matching long-term asset and liability currency exposures
Plain-vanilla purchased FX options for downside protection on material non-euro exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement and notes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to €1,500 per month of delay and potential administrative strike-off after 3 months

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if annual turnover exceeds €800,000 or total assets exceed €400,000

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual declaration and update of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Bénéficiaires effectifs) to the RCS

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax under the French General Tax Code; qualifying small and medium-sized enterprises may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to ownership and turnover conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying patent and other eligible intellectual-property income may benefit from a 10% rate under the French intellectual-property regime. Certain newly created businesses and businesses located in eligible priority zones may qualify for conditional exemptions or reductions. France generally permits indefinite carryforward of tax losses, subject to the annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million; carryback is generally limited to the preceding fiscal year and capped at EUR 1 million. The prescribed five-year field is not the substantive French statutory expiry rule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional account or by EDI-TDFC, together with the applicable tax package, normally Forms 2050-SD through 2059-G-SD for the normal regime or Form 2033-A-SD through 2033-G-SD for the simplified regime.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly corporate income tax installments generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, followed by a balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and tax package are generally due within three months after the fiscal year-end, or by the second business day following 1 May for a financial year ending on 31 December. The final balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the balance is generally due by 15 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, fiscal year beginning and ending dates, legal form as SAS, tax regime, and applicable tax-consolidation status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French-resident SAS reports its French legal entity and French fiscal period. A non-resident company files only where it has a French permanent establishment or another French-source filing obligation and must identify the relevant French establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065-SD, taxable profit or loss and corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result, tax adjustments, taxable result, tax rate application, foreign tax credits where available, installments, credits, and final amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French permanent establishment reports the profit attributable to the French activity under the authorized OECD approach and excludes profits not attributable to France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assets, liabilities, equity, turnover, operating expenses, financial income and expenses, exceptional items, depreciation, provisions, and accounting profit or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A permanent establishment must provide accounts or an equivalent allocation showing French assets, liabilities, revenues, costs, and head-office allocations. Unsupported management charges are high-risk items.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions reconciling statutory accounting profit to taxable profit, including non-deductible expenses, tax depreciation differences, provisions, and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: French-source income and expenses must be isolated. Head-office charges require a demonstrable business purpose, allocation key, supporting documentation, and arm's-length basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening tax losses, losses utilized during the year, current-year loss, and closing balance, subject to the annual utilization limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A permanent establishment may use losses only to the extent attributable to the French taxable activity and subject to French continuity and utilization rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, preferential deductions, exempt or reduced-rate income, and other tax adjustments affecting the corporate income tax computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident may claim only incentives legally available to its French taxable presence and must satisfy any EU, treaty, substance, and documentation conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2572-SD, corporate income tax installments and balance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly installments, tax credits, prior payments, balance due, refund request, and payment reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French permanent establishment pays tax attributable to its French profits. A non-resident without a French taxable presence normally does not file Form 2572 solely because it receives French-source payments subject to withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends, interest, royalties, and other investment income subject to French withholding, together with withholding collected and remitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French payer or withholding agent generally files and pays the withholding. Treaty exemption or reduction requires timely documentation, beneficial-owner analysis, and the prescribed relief-at-source or refund procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income, foreign tax credits, and supporting computations where the relevant French tax-credit mechanism applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A permanent establishment must disclose foreign-source items only where legally relevant to the French tax computation and must retain foreign tax certificates and treaty support.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% after formal notice and potentially 80% for fraudulent or abusive conduct. Late payment generally attracts interest of 0.20% per month and, in applicable cases, a 5% late-payment surcharge. Deliberate concealment, inaccurate returns, or abusive arrangements may trigger additional tax penalties of 40% or 80%, criminal prosecution, and loss of tax benefits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: French electronic corporate income tax package through impots.gouv.fr professional account or EDI-TDFC; payment and installment instructions through the corporate tax payment service.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Installments are generally due on the 15th day of March, June, September, and December. The last installment may be adjusted under the statutory annual installment rules. The balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year corporate income tax liability or estimated current-year liability used to calculate installments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only the tax attributable to the French taxable entity or permanent establishment; do not include unrelated foreign-company liabilities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, tax account reference, payment period, amount, and authorized bank account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The payment must identify the French entity or establishment and be made through an accepted French tax-payment channel or authorized payment intermediary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total annual liability less installments, credits, withholding, and eligible offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance to Form 2065 and retain a payment ledger, tax-credit evidence, and reconciliation of any withholding suffered.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Missed installments may produce late-payment interest and a 5% surcharge, together with collection measures. Material underpayment may also create an estimated-assessment risk, cash-tax exposure, and enhanced penalties where the underpayment is deliberate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident legal entity are generally subject to 25% withholding tax under domestic law, subject to treaty relief and exemptions. A qualifying EU parent company may obtain exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive implementation where the minimum holding, holding-period, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. Dividends paid to non-resident individuals are generally subject to a 12.8% domestic withholding rate, with separate social-contribution rules potentially relevant to French residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the beneficial owner should provide the payer with the applicable French tax-residence certificate and the prescribed Forms 5000 and, where relevant, Form 5001 for dividends, Form 5002 for interest, or Form 5003 for royalties. The payer must verify beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, anti-abuse conditions, minimum holding requirements, and limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test issues. If relief at source is unavailable, the payer generally withholds at the domestic rate and the recipient files the applicable refund documentation with the French tax administration within the statutory period. A certificate of residence must normally be current for the payment period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties and similar remuneration paid to non-residents are generally subject to 25% withholding tax under Article 182 B of the French General Tax Code, subject to treaty reduction or exemption and EU-specific rules. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax under domestic law, except for specific statutory situations, including payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions or territories and certain instrument-specific rules. Tax treaties commonly provide a 0% to 15% maximum royalty rate and a 0% to 15% maximum interest rate, but the applicable treaty, beneficial ownership, residence, and anti-abuse conditions must be verified.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 threshold for the principal large-enterprise transfer-pricing documentation obligations under French law, based on turnover or gross assets, or where the enterprise is controlled by, controls, or belongs to a group containing an entity meeting the statutory threshold. A Local File and Master File may also be required under specific group and transaction circumstances. Country-by-Country Reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a separate UAE-style standalone Economic Substance Regulation regime. Substance is nevertheless material under the French general anti-abuse rule, beneficial-ownership principles, EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive measures, controlled-foreign-company rules, interest limitation rules, treaty anti-abuse provisions, and the principal-purpose test. A French SAS performing fulfillment, kitting, packaging, or 3PL functions should maintain real personnel, premises or operational capacity, inventory and process controls, commercial risk evidence, decision-making records, and contemporaneous intercompany pricing support. Artificial arrangements lacking commercial substance may be recharacterized, denied treaty benefits, or challenged under abuse-of-law rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing turnover, fabricating expenses, omitting taxable income, falsifying inventory, using false invoices, or deliberately understating French taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, penalties generally ranging from 40% to 80% of the evaded tax, and criminal sanctions. Ordinary tax fraud may result in up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine for an individual; aggravated cases may result in up to seven years' imprisonment and a EUR 3 million fine, subject to statutory aggravating conditions. Corporate criminal fines can be increased under the rules applicable to legal persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director or de facto manager may incur personal criminal liability, civil liability for misconduct in management, and tax-director liability where deliberate or fraudulent conduct caused non-payment. A court may impose asset seizure, disqualification from management, or judicial travel restrictions where legally justified; travel bans are not automatic. The corporate veil is not pierced merely because the SAS owes tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register or report French VAT, claiming fictitious input VAT, issuing false invoices, misclassifying domestic fulfillment services as exports, or participating in missing-trader transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, repayment of improperly claimed credits, 40% or 80% penalties depending on conduct, late-payment interest, joint and several recovery in qualifying cases, and criminal prosecution for fraud, forgery, or money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and finance officers may face criminal liability, personal tax-recovery proceedings for fraudulent conduct, management bans, asset seizure, and imprisonment where the evidence establishes intentional participation or knowing facilitation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management, logistics, royalty, financing, or procurement fees; allocating French profits to a low-substance affiliate; or failing to document related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of French taxable income, withholding-tax exposure, interest limitation or deduction denial, penalties for inadequate documentation, and possible 40% or 80% penalties where the conduct is deliberate or abusive. The French tax administration may apply the arm's-length principle and abuse-of-law provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for deliberate management misconduct, fraudulent tax conduct, or knowingly approving unsupported transactions. Routine transfer-pricing errors do not automatically create personal criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, artificial substance, and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a French SAS with nominal directors, no genuine operational capacity, circular payments, conduit dividend or royalty arrangements, or an arrangement principally designed to obtain treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, withholding at domestic rates, reassessment under the general anti-abuse rule, penalties of up to 80% in serious abusive cases, interest, and potential criminal consequences if false records or fraudulent declarations are used.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil claims, tax-recovery actions, criminal prosecution for fraud or money laundering where applicable, management disqualification, and seizure of proceeds. No automatic veil piercing or automatic travel ban follows solely from insufficient substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, concealing beneficial owners, structuring payments to evade controls, processing proceeds of crime, or failing to identify and escalate suspicious transactions where a regulated obligation applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering may result in imprisonment and fines, with aggravated penalties for organized or repeated conduct. Proceeds may be confiscated, and the company may face criminal fines, dissolution, prohibition from conducting activities, or exclusion from public contracts where ordered by a court.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face imprisonment, personal fines, confiscation, professional disqualification, and judicial travel restrictions. Liability requires personal participation, authorization, complicity, or legally established management fault; corporate status does not immunize an individual.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared foreign accounts and cross-border reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to report reportable foreign bank, payment, or digital-asset accounts, concealing foreign income, or misusing payment platforms to avoid French tax reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, tax reassessment, late-payment interest, enhanced penalties for concealed assets, and potential criminal tax-fraud proceedings where deliberate concealment is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The individual who owns, controls, or deliberately administers the undisclosed account may be personally assessed and prosecuted. Directors are not automatically liable for accounts belonging solely to the company unless they participated in or authorized the concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs, import, and fulfillment documentation fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misstating customs value, origin, tariff classification, importer of record, or inventory movements; using false commercial invoices; or avoiding import VAT and customs duties through incorrect kitting documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of duties and import VAT, customs fines, seizure or forfeiture of goods, suspension of customs simplifications, and criminal prosecution for smuggling or document fraud in serious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and customs representatives may incur personal liability where they knowingly submit false declarations or instruct unlawful import practices. The company may also face joint liability, loss of customs authorizations, and exclusion from trusted-trader programs.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Accounting, corporate governance, and insolvency misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Keeping incomplete accounts, destroying accounting records, distributing profits while insolvent, continuing operations while cessation of payments is concealed, or preferring related parties before insolvency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Accounting sanctions, rejection of deductions, civil claims, insolvency clawback, management bans, contribution to insufficient assets, bankruptcy-related penalties, and criminal sanctions for concealment or fraudulent bankruptcy.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: SAS officers and de facto managers may be ordered to contribute to company liabilities where management misconduct caused an asset shortfall and may face personal civil restitution, disqualification, asset seizure, or imprisonment for intentional insolvency offenses.
